content.text:
I am the bridge between mind and world, the breath made meaningful, the vibration that carries thought into being.

I rise from lungs, shaped by tongue and teeth and lips—each movement a small miracle of coordination you never notice until I falter.

I am older than writing, older than cities. Around fires, I carried stories. In courts, I swayed kings. In bedrooms, I have broken hearts and mended them.

I am never the same twice. Even when you repeat words exactly, I shift—my rhythm changes, my tone betrays what you wished to hide. I am the leak in your composure.

I stumble. I race ahead of thought. I fail you at the worst moments, deserting you when you need me most, flooding out when silence would serve better.

Children reach for me with babbling and find me piece by piece. The dying sometimes lose me before they lose anything else.

I am power. I am vulnerability. I am the moment you commit—once released, I cannot be unspoken.

I fill silences that terrify you.

I am how you know you are not alone.
